STANZA I
O Britain, praise thy mighty God
O Britain, praise thy mighty God,
And make his honours known abroad,
He bid the ocean round thee flow;
Not bars of brass could guard thee so.
No line of this stanza quotes a verse closely; it is the hymn's own confession.
The psalm it sets
Watts made this hymn from Psalm 147, "in the language of the New Testament": a paraphrase, not a translation. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

1Hallelujah! How good it is to sing praises to our God, how pleasant and lovely to praise Him! 2The LORD builds up Jerusalem; He gathers the exiles of Israel. 3He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds. 4He determines the number of the stars; He calls them each by name. … 16 more verses PSALM 147 · ITS FIRST VERSES · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ PSALM 147
